commenti.body: This hasn't opened in my area yet.  However, the old summary sounds a lot like Spike Lee's Bamboozled.  And strangely enough, the flaws you list in this film were flaws in Spike's film as well.
Damnit you should've marked your comment as a spoiler. haven't seen bamboozled yet

I liked the meta aspects of the ending but agree that the A plot didn’t get enough attention. It almost felt like two different movies got combined into one. And it made the A Plot feel a little bit more of a gimmick than something earned and necessary. Though there is a dovetail  between the point of Plot A (“what is a Black story?”) and B/C/etc. 

I just wish all the trailers didn’t show all the main scenes used in the A plot. 

So while it’s good, it’s not great in the way I had hoped.

It was okay. I didn't think it was as daring or absurdist to follow its premise all the way to the end.

There has been a trend of African American surrealism becoming more popular over the past decade or so. American Fiction almost gets there but is a bit tamer than earlier works such as Sorry to Bother You.
Sorry to Bother You was great except I will never emotionally recover from the horse plot.

Agree wholeheartedly with you. It felt uneven whenever it shifted to the subplots. Granted, the subplots were meant to ground the character in reality, it was not well written. Would have loved to see more of his siblings stories though if it were more artfully done.
